summary.title: Visualizing Tech Company Layoffs in 2022
summary.one_liner: Learn which major tech companies (Meta, Twitter, Byju's, Peloton) cut jobs in 2022, the economic reasons given, and why the layoffs did not signal broader US economic weakness.
keywords: tech jobs share of us employment
why are tech companies laying off
takeaways: Meta, Twitter, Byju's and Peloton were among the high-profile tech layoffs in 2022, with Meta and Twitter making the largest cuts.
Stated reasons include economic uncertainty and poor performance; Goldman Sachs Research links higher interest rates to greater pressure on tech profits.
Shrinking ad budgets and the crypto market collapse were also cited as factors (e.g., Twitter, Snapchat, Coinbase, Kraken).
Despite the layoffs, US payroll data beat expectations and unemployment was near a half-century low, partly because tech jobs are under 3% of US employment.
Data came from trueup.io, which tracks US and international tech layoffs; the article was written in late 2022.
summary.summary: This Visual Capitalist infographic article, written around late 2022, surveys the wave of tech layoffs that year using data from trueup.io. It profiles high-profile cuts at Meta, Twitter (after Elon Musk's takeover), Byju's in India, and Peloton, which cut staff in stages. It then explains the reasons given, including higher interest rates, shrinking ad budgets, and the crypto downturn, and argues that the layoffs did not appear to signal broader economic trouble. The page also contains unrelated 2026 teaser content (property taxes, Halloween candy) that was ignored.
